overview: Impact of LPG on governance and statutory, regulatory and quasi-judicial bodies: 9 official questions (2010-2024), 5 of them in 2023-24 as statement-based items testing a body's legal basis, composition, procedure and number of benches. Older items are Lokayukta/Lokpal firsts (one deleted, one key disputed).

possibility.what_they_ask: post-1991 hiring and delivery trends (outsourcing, contractualisation, PPP, regulators replacing licensing)
founding Act and year; number of notified minorities; Lokayukta tenure changes; first State with a Lokayukta

possibility.evidence: 1 Q: 2023; related APPSC items on SEBI and IRDAI
possibility.what_they_ask: Act that created it and its composition

possibility.angle: Quasi-judicial and advisory bodies (CAT, NGT, Law Commission)
possibility.what_they_ask: statutory or not; bound by CPC or not; benches/sittings; whom it reports to

traps.trap: [CPC binding] Tribunal said to be bound by the Code of Civil Procedure
traps.spot: Statement 'X is bound by the procedure of CPC 1908'
traps.fix: CAT and NGT are not bound by CPC; they follow natural justice
traps.pyq: NGT 'bound by CPC' false [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#53]; CAT 'not bound by CPC' true [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#34]

traps.spot: Number of benches, members or notified communities
traps.fix: NGT five sittings; six notified minorities (Jains 2014); CCI chairperson + 2 to 6 members
traps.pyq: 'six places of sitting' false [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#53]; 'five religious communities' false [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#55]; 'chairperson and five members' false [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#57]

traps.fix: CAT has judicial and administrative members
traps.pyq: Statement II false → 'I, III, IV and V' [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#34]

traps.trap: Advisory body labelled quasi-judicial and given wrong recipient
traps.spot: Law Commission statements on status, recipient, Parliament, suo motu
traps.fix: Executive, non-statutory, advisory; advises the Law Ministry; reports laid before Parliament; can act suo motu

techniques.name: Four-field body card
techniques.how: [Basis / composition / procedure / appeal] For each body memorise: constitutional, statutory or executive; members; CPC-bound or not; where appeals go.
techniques.example: NGT: 2010 Act; not CPC-bound; 5 sittings → only statement I correct [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#53]

techniques.name: Number check
techniques.how: In statement items, a precise number is the usual altered element; verify each number before the qualitative parts.
techniques.example: NCM: 1992 Act true; 'five' communities wrong (six) → 'I and III only' [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#55]

techniques.name: State-Act variation for Lokayuktas
techniques.how: Lokayuktas come from separate State Acts, so tenure and powers differ; tie a news change to the State that amended its Act.
techniques.example: Tenure cut from 8 to 5 years → Rajasthan (2019) [group1-prelims-2019-paper2#96]

confusions.remember: Central services, AIS vs State services
environment, 5 sittings, appeal to SC vs service matters, appeal to HC bench
Competition Act 2002 vs SEBI Act 1992 (body 1988, statutory 1992)
third-party agency supplies staff vs government hires directly on contract

anchors: NGT: NGT Act 2010; principal bench New Delhi + Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata, Chennai
NCM Act 1992; six notified minorities (Jains added 2014)
Competition Act 2002, amended 2007; chairperson + 2 to 6 members
Lokpal: first Bill 1968, Act 2013, in force 2014
Law Commission: executive body, first post-independence 1955
checklist: Is the body constitutional, statutory or executive?
To whom does it report or advise?
For State bodies, name the State whose Act changed.
